knowledge_point.title: Computing Line Integrals With Respect to X and Y Along Circles and Ellipses

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following definite integrals is equivalent to

$$
\int_C\left(x^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(2 x y\right)\,\mathrm{d}y
$$

where $C$ is the arc of the ellipse $4 x^{2} + 9 y^{2}=36$, traversed clockwise from $\left(0,-2\right)$ to $\left(-3,0\right)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametrization $x=3 \cos{\left(t \right)}$, $y=2 \sin{\left(t \right)}$. The endpoints and clockwise traversal give $t$ from $\frac{3 \pi}{2}$ to $\pi$.

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathrm{d}x &=- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,\mathrm{d}t \\ \mathrm{d}y &=2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,\mathrm{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute the coordinates and their signed differentials. Let $U$ be the contribution from the $\mathrm{d}x$ term and $V$ the contribution from the $\mathrm{d}y$ term:

$$
\begin{aligned}U(t) &=\left(9 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right) \\ V(t) &=\left(12 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

$$
I=\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{\pi}[U(t)+V(t)]\,\mathrm{d}t
$$

$$
I=\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{\pi}\left(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)\,\mathrm{d}t
$$

This is the required equivalent definite integral.

knowledge_point.title: Computing Line Integrals With Respect to X and Y Along Circles and Ellipses

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate

$$
\int_C\left(\frac{2 x}{y}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)\,\mathrm{d}y
$$

where $C$ is the arc of the circle $x^{2} + y^{2}=1$, traversed clockwise from $\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)$ to $\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},- \frac{1}{2}\right)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametrization $x=\cos{\left(t \right)}$, $y=\sin{\left(t \right)}$. The endpoints and clockwise traversal give $t$ from $\frac{5 \pi}{4}$ to $\frac{7 \pi}{6}$.

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathrm{d}x &=- \sin{\left(t \right)}\,\mathrm{d}t \\ \mathrm{d}y &=\cos{\left(t \right)}\,\mathrm{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute the coordinates and their signed differentials. Let $U$ be the contribution from the $\mathrm{d}x$ term and $V$ the contribution from the $\mathrm{d}y$ term:

$$
\begin{aligned}U(t) &=\left(\frac{2 \cos{\left(t \right)}}{\sin{\left(t \right)}}\right)\left(- \sin{\left(t \right)}\right) \\ V(t) &=\left(\frac{\sin{\left(t \right)}}{\cos{\left(t \right)}}\right)\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

$$
I=\int_{\frac{5 \pi}{4}}^{\frac{7 \pi}{6}}[U(t)+V(t)]\,\mathrm{d}t
$$

The arc stays inside one quadrant, so $x$ and $y$ are nonzero. Cancel the sine and cosine factors to obtain

$$
I=\int_{\frac{5 \pi}{4}}^{\frac{7 \pi}{6}}\left(\sin{\left(t \right)} - 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\,\mathrm{d}t
$$

An antiderivative of the displayed integrand is $F(t)=- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}$. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}I &= \left[- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}\right]_{\frac{5 \pi}{4}}^{\frac{7 \pi}{6}} \\ &= \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + 1\right)-\left(\frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\ &= - \frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + 1\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Computing Line Integrals With Respect to X and Y Along Circles and Ellipses

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate

$$
\int_C\left(x - 2 y\right)\,\mathrm{d}x+\left(2 x + 2 y\right)\,\mathrm{d}y
$$

where $C$ is the arc of the ellipse $4 x^{2} + 9 y^{2}=36$, traversed clockwise from $\left(0,-2\right)$ to $\left(-3,0\right)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametrization $x=3 \cos{\left(t \right)}$, $y=2 \sin{\left(t \right)}$. The endpoints and clockwise traversal give $t$ from $\frac{3 \pi}{2}$ to $\pi$.

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathrm{d}x &=- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,\mathrm{d}t \\ \mathrm{d}y &=2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,\mathrm{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute the coordinates and their signed differentials. Let $U$ be the contribution from the $\mathrm{d}x$ term and $V$ the contribution from the $\mathrm{d}y$ term:

$$
\begin{aligned}U(t) &=\left(- 4 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right) \\ V(t) &=\left(4 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 6 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\left(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

$$
I=\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{\pi}[U(t)+V(t)]\,\mathrm{d}t
$$

Using $\sin^2t+\cos^2t=1$, combine the terms to obtain

$$
I=\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{\pi}\left(- \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + 12\right)\,\mathrm{d}t
$$

An antiderivative of the displayed integrand is $F(t)=12 t - \frac{\sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}}{2}$. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}I &= \left[12 t - \frac{\sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}}{2}\right]_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{\pi} \\ &= \left(12 \pi\right)-\left(- \frac{1}{2} + 18 \pi\right) \\ &= \frac{1}{2} - 6 \pi\end{aligned}
$$
